chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated to me from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام concerning a man who is afflicted with janābah while he is in an open desert, and he has only one garment upon him, and semen has affected his garment. He said: "He performs tayammum, removes his garment, sits in a gathered posture, and performs salat, gesturing by indication."

key_terms.ثَوْبٌ وَاحِدٌ: a single garment with no alternative clothing available
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.مَنِيٌّ: semen, treated here as causing impurity to the garment
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.يَطْرَحُ ثَوْبَهُ: he removes or casts off his garment
key_terms.يُومِئُ إِيمَاءً: he indicates the prayer motions by gesture

ai.seo_question: What should a person in janābah do if his only garment is contaminated and he is alone in the desert?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person in janābah who is in an isolated place and has only one garment that has been contaminated with semen. He is instructed to perform tayammum, remove the impure garment, and perform salat while seated in a gathered posture, indicating the prayer movements by gesture.
